clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the next year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and kept his distance from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and was warned at work, then separated from Celeste; your mother lay awake over them both; and your brother Callum had ear infections all winter. Your grandmother took a job at the library by May 1979 and her functioning came back up; the shifts in the months after the death moved from person to person as the family reacted.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984–1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother being ordered to bed for the rest of her pregnancy in March 1984: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep the house, then argued with your father over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it; your sister Ines would not sleep without your father by the bed. Your sister was born in September, and your father's functioning came back as he adjusted to the new baby; the shifts cluster in these months as the household managed your mother's absence.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, over the next decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and all her appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news of her; he and your uncle Lyle argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather developed chest pains; your grandmother fell and walked with a frame, then could no longer dress herself or stand; your father and uncle Lyle stopped visiting their parents; your mother took her to the clinic twice a week, and your aunt Mavis came to stay one week in four to nurse her sister; your uncle Anton drank most evenings; your aunt Pearl had panic spells at the wheel. Your grandmother had a good summer in 1994, then declined again; your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left her side. This long climb over years, each step bringing a new shift with only partial relief between them, tracks the family's reaction to her progressive illness.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for a job at the mines in May 1999: your father and Callum argued most nights over his plans to go north; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere, even to work. By August 2000, Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams; the shifts belong to your mother and father's struggle with his departure and its pull on your sister.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within the year: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night, stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May, dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark. You stopped returning your mother's calls. By November you took a job at the garden centre and slept through the night again; these are all shifts of yours, and no one else's shows in these months.
